question: Participation of the EU at the 10th Conference of the Parties to the WHO Framework Convention on Tobacco Control in February 2024

The EU legislative framework for tobacco control is in an ongoing process of revision and all of the Member States, as well as the European institutions, work together to ensure a balanced, smart and effective set of regulations which mirrors the democratic consensus within the EU.

The 10th Conference of the Parties to the WHO Framework Convention on Tobacco Control (COP 10) will see the Member States represented by the Commission. The Commission should respect the fact that the resolutions taken at COP 10 will have a crucial impact on the future of the legislative framework for tobacco control.

The EU legislative body, namely the Council, should therefore be taken into account and consulted during the negotiations. Furthermore, Parliament should be continuously informed about the process. 1.
How will the Commission ensure that the Council’s position is heard and respected during inperson negotiations at COP 10?
How exactly is the term ‘refinement’, as used by the Commission, defined and who is in charge of deciding what refinement of the mandate means and what substantive change this entails?
How will the Commission ensure that Parliament is informed in a comprehensive and timely manner about the EU position and the proceedings at COP 10 during the negotiations themselves?
answer: The positions of the EU at the tenth session of the Conference of the Parties (COP10) to the World Health Organisation (WHO) Framework Convention on Tobacco Control (FCTC) have been established by the Council of the EU, on a proposal from the Commission, in accordance with the legal procedures and safeguards provided by the Treaties (1).

In accordance with the Treaties, the European Parliament does not take part in the decision-making process for establishing the Union positions in international bodies, and is informed by the Council (Article 218(10) of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (2)). The EU and all its Member States are Parties to the FCTC.

Decisions at the Conference of the Parties (COP) to the FCTC are taken by the Parties to the FCTC, in line with the Rules of Procedure of the COP (3). The COP’s task is to keep the implementation of the FCTC under regular review and take the decisions necessary to promote its effective implementation.

The EU can only make a statement in those cases where it is competent and there is a position which has been agreed in accordance with the relevant Treaty provisions. Member States and the Commission coordinate their action to the fullest extent possible in accordance with Article 2 of the Council decision establishing a Union position and the Treaties.

All decisions of the COP are publicly available on the WHO FCTC website (4). The Commission is currently evaluating the EU legislative framework for tobacco control. Any possible future Commission proposal in this area will be prepared in compliance with the Better Regulation principles (5).

See Council Decision (EU) 2024/649 of 15 November 2023 on the position to be taken on behalf of the Union at the 10th session of the Conference of the Parties to the WHO Framework Convention on Tobacco Control (OJ L, 2024/649, 19.02.2024). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/resource.html?uri=cellar:2bf140bf-a3f8-4ab2-b506-fd71826e6da6.0023.
